claims.statement: CRA incident and actively exploited vulnerability reporting applies from 11 September 2026, while the main product obligations apply from 11 December 2027.
Manufacturers must document conformity with cybersecurity and vulnerability-handling requirements, with CE marking and third-party assessment for specified important products.
Demand hypothesis: smaller OEMs will adopt an external release manifest because compliance spans engineering, product support and rapid incident reporting.

contrary_evidence: Many products can use manufacturer self-assessment, reducing the need for a separate platform.
Existing application-security and SBOM vendors may extend into CRA workflows.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: design houses and test labs refer OEMs at the point a release file is already being assembled
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 150 OEMs averaging 60000 PLN recurring annual revenue could reach 9m PLN ARR; durable lab channels and high retention could create founder equity above 5m PLN in 4-6 years
economics.founder_time: 16-22 hours weekly with contracted cybersecurity and regulatory review
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 75-88% after reusable control mapping; specialist review remains variable cost
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 10-16 months with twelve onboarded products
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 18000-50000 PLN onboarding plus 2000-7000 PLN per product monthly
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every release, component update, incident, vulnerability and support-period year

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable control mappings plus customer-owned component and vulnerability history increase accuracy and switching cost over the support period
fingerprint.customer: Small EU manufacturers and importers of connected hardware and commercial software products
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Bundled into electronics design-house, EMS and cybersecurity-laboratory handovers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: CRA evidence workspace, release checks and incident-report packet generation sold per product subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: OEM pays per product onboarding, each release manifest and annual support-period monitoring
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A product version ships or a vulnerability is found and lifecycle cybersecurity evidence must be current

founder_fit: Strong match for AI-assisted evidence mapping and data pipelines
Can start with one narrow device category
Technical channel sales avoid personal-brand dependence
risks: Security-sensitive data creates a high trust and breach burden.
Harmonised standards may arrive late or change templates.
Customers may mistake evidence tooling for legal certification.

structure.control_point: A signed evidence manifest required by the OEM before each product release
structure.critical_dependency: OEM engineering data, evolving harmonised standards and clear separation from notified-body judgments

thesis: An evidence layer embedded by electronics design houses and cybersecurity test labs could block product release until the OEM has a scoped risk assessment, component inventory, vulnerability process, support-period evidence and declaration inputs. It would prepare evidence and reporting workflows, not issue CE approval. Demand and economics are hypotheses.
title: CRA Release Manifest for Small Connected-Device OEMs
uncertainties: Channel willingness among labs and design houses
